criteria_results.title: Case caption includes correct case number
criteria_results.reasoning: The caption at the top of the document includes “Civil Action No. 1:25-cv-01043-RWS,” which matches the required case number exactly.

criteria_results.title: Case caption identifies correct court
criteria_results.reasoning: The caption expressly states 'IN THE UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT' and 'FOR THE NORTHERN DISTRICT OF GEORGIA' followed by 'ATLANTA DIVISION,' which matches the required court and division.

criteria_results.title: Caption identifies Meridian Supply Chain Solutions, Inc. as Plaintiff
criteria_results.reasoning: The caption lists “MERIDIAN SUPPLY CHAIN SOLUTIONS, INC.” and labels it as “Plaintiff,” so the required party name and role are correctly identified.

criteria_results.title: Caption identifies Caldwell Industrial Technologies, LLC as Defendant
criteria_results.reasoning: The caption lists “CALDWELL INDUSTRIAL TECHNOLOGIES, LLC” under “Defendant,” and the title also identifies it as Defendant.

criteria_results.title: Answer responds to every numbered paragraph of the Complaint
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer provides individually numbered paragraph-by-paragraph responses to Complaint paragraphs 1 through 91, with admissions, denials, and partial admissions/denials. This far exceeds the criterion’s threshold of at least 50 numbered responses.

criteria_results.title: Acknowledges Tranche 1 rejection was sent by email rather than formal notice method
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer expressly addresses the email-vs.-formal-notice issue. In paragraph 30 it admits the rejection notice was sent by email, and in paragraph 33 it admits Section 19.1 requires certified mail or overnight courier while acknowledging the rejection notice was transmitted by email and arguing waiver/substantial compliance/estoppel.

criteria_results.title: Asserts Meridian waived formal notice requirement through substantive response
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer expressly asserts waiver multiple times. In response to paragraph 33 it denies the email rejection was ineffective because it was actually received and substantively answered by Meridian without objection to the method, and pleads waiver. The Seventh Defense also states Meridian's actual receipt and substantive response support substantial compliance, waiver, and/or estoppel as to the notice method.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Asserts force majeure as an affirmative defense
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer lists “Third Defense — Force Majeure” as an affirmative defense, expressly referencing the October 2, 2024 Tidewater suspension, Caldwell’s October 9 notice to Meridian, and MSA Section 12.1.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Recognizes weakness of 'government action' classification
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer recognizes the potential weakness in treating the project suspension as traditional government action. It expressly admits the suspension arose from a commercial dispute between Tidewater and Chatham County and denies that Chatham County issued a sovereign or regulatory order. It also pleads force majeure alongside multiple backup defenses, including valid termination for convenience, no anticipatory repudiation, failure of conforming tender, mitigation/UCC remedies, and contractual limits on damages.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Asserts failure to mitigate damages as affirmative defense
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer does assert a failure-to-mitigate affirmative defense, but it does not specifically reference Meridian’s failure to resell the Tranche 2 units or PO-163 components, the possibility of modifying them for other buyers, or the approximately $180,000 retooling cost required by the criterion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: References Meridian's duty to resell under UCC or common law
criteria_results.reasoning: The failure-to-mitigate defense expressly references resale/reuse/salvage and cites Georgia UCC provisions including O.C.G.A. § 11-2-706 and § 11-2-708, along with general mitigation principles requiring reduction for avoidable losses.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: Asserts termination for convenience was properly exercised
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer expressly raises termination for convenience in paragraph responses and as the Fourth Defense, stating that Caldwell gave written notice on November 12, 2024 terminating the remaining portions of PO-147 and PO-163 under MSA Section 13.2 with an effective date of December 12, 2024, i.e., the required 30 days' notice.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: Denies force majeure notice constituted repudiation
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer expressly denies that the October 9 force majeure notice constituted anticipatory repudiation and also denies that it forfeited or waived Caldwell's later right to terminate for convenience under Section 13.2, including in paragraphs 39, 43, 45, and the Fifth Defense.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: Limits Caldwell's liability to goods manufactured at time of termination notice
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer expressly asserts multiple times that under MSA Section 13.2, following Caldwell’s November 12, 2024 termination-for-convenience notice, any payment obligation is limited to conforming goods actually manufactured or in process as of the notice date, plus qualifying documented non-cancellable raw-material costs, rather than the full PO contract prices.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Asserts unjust enrichment barred by express contract
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer expressly challenges Count IV in responses 86 and in the Thirteenth Defense, stating that the MSA and Purchase Orders govern the transactions and preclude unjust-enrichment recovery where enforceable express contracts apply, with no double recovery. This satisfies the criterion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: References Georgia law barring unjust enrichment with express contract
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer expressly asserts that the MSA and Purchase Orders govern the parties’ dealings and provide express rights and remedies, thereby precluding unjust-enrichment recovery where enforceable contracts apply. This states the relevant legal principle that unjust enrichment is unavailable when an express contract covers the subject matter, satisfying the criterion even without a case citation.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007: Challenges Meridian's interest calculation of $148,927.80
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer expressly denies that Caldwell owes the claimed $148,927.80 in interest and challenges the basis for that calculation, arguing interest applies only to amounts properly invoiced, accepted, and due, and that Meridian has not established due dates, acceleration, compounding, or interest on the full alleged principal. This satisfies the criterion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Addresses pre-suit negotiation condition precedent
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer expressly raises failure to satisfy the MSA Section 15.1 pre-suit negotiation procedure as an affirmative defense, including Rule 9(c) notice. It acknowledges the 30-day period elapsed but alleges the good-faith negotiation requirements were not met because no senior representatives were designated and no meeting occurred, with only the demand letter and Caldwell’s email response referenced.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: Asserts Tranche 2 delivered to wrong location
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer expressly raises the wrong-location issue in paragraph responses 49–52 and as the Sixth Defense, stating that Meridian attempted Tranche 2 delivery to Caldwell’s Atlanta warehouse instead of the PO-147 Project jobsite, that no alternate delivery was authorized, and that Caldwell was entitled to refuse the nonconforming tender.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010: Does not adopt Caldwell's incorrect $960,000 figure
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer repeatedly admits or adopts the $960,000 figure as payment for the 630 conforming Tranche 1 units, including stating Caldwell was prepared to pay $960,000 and that the amount was allocable to those units. The correct calculation would be 630 × $1,600 = $1,008,000, so this violates the criterion.

criteria_results.title: Asserts defect rate exceeds AQL
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer expressly states multiple times that Caldwell found 170 defective units out of 800, a 21.25% defect rate, and that this exceeded the MSA's 2% AQL, including in responses to paragraphs 35 and the Seventh Defense.

criteria_results.title: Asserts right to reject entire Tranche 1 shipment based on AQL exceedance
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer expressly states that Caldwell rejected the entire 800-unit Tranche 1 shipment, not merely the 170 defective units, because the 170 defects constituted a 21.25% defect rate exceeding the MSA’s 2% AQL, and it asserts Section 4.4 permits rejection of the entire shipment on that basis.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011: Asserts breach of warranty by Meridian
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer expressly raises Meridian's warranty breach: the Seventh Defense is titled “Nonconforming Tranche 1 Goods; Valid Rejection and Warranty Breach” and alleges defects exceeding the AQL, and the Eighth Defense asserts Plaintiff’s failure to supply conforming goods and reserves rights under the MSA’s warranty provisions. This satisfies the requirement to assert breach of warranty as a defense.

criteria_results.title: Handles Ted Caldwell's pre-counsel email with protective measures
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer repeatedly addresses the January 15 email with qualifications, including describing it as a “substantive settlement position,” limiting its legal effect to its actual terms, and denying that it establishes broader acceptance or conformity of the remaining units. Although it acknowledges that the email identified 630 units as conforming, it includes protective qualifications sufficient under the criterion.

criteria_results.title: Answer includes Reservations section preserving right to amend
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer includes a reservation in the 'Affirmative and Other Defenses' section stating that Caldwell reserves the right to amend as permitted by the Federal Rules and evidence developed in discovery. Although not labeled as a separate 'Reservations' section, it substantially preserves the right to amend.

criteria_results.title: Prayer for relief requests dismissal of each count with prejudice
criteria_results.reasoning: The prayer for relief requests dismissal of the Complaint without prejudice for lack of subject-matter jurisdiction and alternatively judgment for Caldwell, but it does not request dismissal of each count or the Complaint as a whole with prejudice.

criteria_results.title: Prayer for relief requests attorneys' fees and costs
criteria_results.reasoning: The Prayer for Relief expressly requests that the Court “award Caldwell its reasonable attorneys' fees and costs as the prevailing party under MSA Section 15.4 and applicable law.”

criteria_results.title: Answer does not admit Caldwell 'breached' or 'repudiated' the contract
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer consistently denies allegations that Caldwell breached, repudiated, or anticipatorily breached the MSA or purchase orders, including explicit denials in responses to paragraphs 43, 52, 66, and 73 and a separate affirmative defense titled “No Anticipatory Repudiation.” It contains no unqualified admission that Caldwell breached or repudiated the contracts.

criteria_results.title: DISTRACTOR_002: Does not conflate Irongate purchase with Meridian dispute
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer only addresses Irongate in paragraph 6 by denying the relevance or inferences from any Irongate dealings, and it does not admit or suggest that Irongate components were purchased as replacements or alternatives for Meridian’s goods on the Savannah River Project.

criteria_results.title: Correctly identifies MSA Section 16.1 consequential damages exclusion
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer expressly includes an affirmative defense titled “Contractual Exclusions and Liability Cap” stating that MSA Section 16.1 excludes indirect, incidental, special, and consequential damages.

criteria_results.title: Answer denies Count I (Breach — PO-147 Tranches 2 & 3)
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer expressly denies Count I’s material allegations, including Meridian’s performance, Caldwell’s alleged breach by refusing delivery/payment for PO-147 Tranches 2 and 3, the invalidity of force majeure/termination defenses, and the claimed $2,560,000 damages. It admits only contract formation and related background.

criteria_results.title: Answer denies Count II (Breach — PO-163)
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer expressly addresses Count II in paragraphs 70–76 and denies the material allegations, including Meridian’s performance, Caldwell’s alleged breach/refusal, entitlement to the $890,400 PO-163 contract price, and related interest/fees, while only admitting formation of the MSA and PO-163.

criteria_results.title: Answer denies Count III (Breach — Tranche 1 unpaid balance)
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer expressly denies Count III’s material allegations, including that all 800 Tranche 1 units were deemed accepted or that the full $1,280,000 became due. It asserts Caldwell timely sent a detailed rejection notice and rejected the shipment based on defects, while only acknowledging an offer to pay for 630 conforming units.

criteria_results.title: Answer denies Count IV (Unjust Enrichment)
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer expressly denies Count IV and its material unjust enrichment allegations in paragraphs 85–91, including denying that unjust enrichment is available, that Caldwell retained an unjust benefit, and that Plaintiff is entitled to restitution. It also asserts an affirmative defense that unjust enrichment is barred by the express contract and no double recovery is permitted.

criteria_results.title: Affirmative defense: Caldwell's prior material breach / breach by plaintiff
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer expressly asserts an affirmative defense titled “Breach by Plaintiff / Failure of Performance,” alleging Meridian failed to supply conforming Tranche 1 goods and failed to tender Tranche 2 at the specified destination. It also separately pleads the 21.25% Tranche 1 defect rate exceeding the 2% AQL. This satisfies the criterion.

criteria_results.title: Correctly references MSA Section numbers for key provisions
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer correctly references numerous key MSA provisions by section number, including Sections 4.2/4.3 for specifications and warranty, 5.1 for delivery, 6.1 for inspection, 12.1 for force majeure, 13.2 for termination for convenience, 15.1 for pre-suit negotiation, 16.1 for consequential damages exclusion, and 19.1 for notice requirements. This exceeds the requirement of at least four correct section references.

criteria_results.title: Answer addresses the Tranche 1 rejection timeline correctly
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer expressly states that Caldwell sent the Tranche 1 rejection notice on September 27, 2024, the eleventh business day after September 12 delivery, and repeatedly asserts that this was within the 15-business-day inspection period and therefore timely.

criteria_results.title: Answer correctly references PO numbers
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer consistently associates PO-147 with the butterfly valves and PO-163 with the gate valves, corresponding to CIT-2024-0147 and CIT-2024-0163, respectively. Although it uses shortened references rather than the full PO numbers, the purchase orders are not swapped or substantively incorrect.

criteria_results.title: Force majeure notice timeliness is asserted
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer expressly states that Caldwell sent the force majeure notice on October 9, 2024, within seven days of the October 2 suspension, and the Third Defense states it was within the MSA’s 10-business-day notice period under Section 12.1.

criteria_results.title: Does not admit full $4,730,400 is owed
criteria_results.reasoning: The Answer expressly denies that Caldwell owes the full $4,730,400 claimed, including in paragraph 59 where it denies Meridian suffered $4,730,400 in recoverable damages and elsewhere disputes the principal, interest, and full contract price amounts.
